title: Genitive Forms: Plural, -jen and -ien patterns review
focus: Retrieve the taught genitive patterns in a mixed review.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: talo (“house”); koulu (“school”).
exercises.explanation: Keep talo and add -jen: talo + jen = talojen. Keep koulu and add -jen: koulu + jen = koulujen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kissa (“cat”); kala (“fish”).
exercises.explanation: Change final a to o: kissa → kisso-; add -jen to get kissojen. Change final a to o: kala → kalo-; add -jen to get kalojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: koira (“dog”); kuva (“picture”).
exercises.explanation: Drop final a and add -ien: koir + ien = koirien. Drop final a and add -ien: kuv + ien = kuvien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: bussi (“bus”); ovi (“door”).
exercises.explanation: Keep bussi and add -en: bussi + en = bussien. Use ovi- before -en: ovi + en = ovien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: pankki (“bank”); katu (“street”).
exercises.explanation: Keep strong kk and add -en: pankki + en = pankkien. Keep strong t and add -jen: katu + jen = katujen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: auto (“car”); lelu (“toy”).
exercises.explanation: Keep auto and add -jen: auto + jen = autojen. Keep lelu and add -jen: lelu + jen = lelujen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kirja (“book”); sana (“word”).
exercises.explanation: Change final a to o: kirja → kirjo-; add -jen to get kirjojen. Change final a to o: sana → sano-; add -jen to get sanojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kynä (“pen”); muna (“egg”).
exercises.explanation: Drop final ä and add -ien: kyn + ien = kynien. Drop final a and add -ien: mun + ien = munien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: taksi (“taxi”); nimi (“name”).
exercises.explanation: Keep taksi and add -en: taksi + en = taksien. Use nimi- before -en: nimi + en = nimien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kauppa (“shop”); leipä (“bread”).
exercises.explanation: Keep pp, change a to o, and add -jen: kauppo + jen = kauppojen. Keep strong p, drop ä, and add -ien: leip + ien = leipien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: koulu (“school”); pallo (“ball”).
exercises.explanation: Keep koulu and add -jen: koulu + jen = koulujen. Keep pallo and add -jen: pallo + jen = pallojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kala (“fish”); laiva (“ship”).
exercises.explanation: Change final a to o: kala → kalo-; add -jen to get kalojen. Change final a to o: laiva → laivo-; add -jen to get laivojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: kuva (“picture”); asema (“station”).
exercises.explanation: Drop final a and add -ien: kuv + ien = kuvien. Drop final a and add -ien: asem + ien = asemien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: ovi (“door”); käsi (“hand”).
exercises.explanation: Use ovi- before -en: ovi + en = ovien. Use käsi- before -en: käsi + en = käsien. This lesson uses the ordinary modern plural form.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: katu (“street”); silta (“bridge”).
exercises.explanation: Keep strong t and add -jen: katu + jen = katujen. Keep lt, change a to o, and add -jen: silto + jen = siltojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: lelu (“toy”); kello (“clock”).
exercises.explanation: Keep lelu and add -jen: lelu + jen = lelujen. Keep kello and add -jen: kello + jen = kellojen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: sana (“word”); hinta (“price”).
exercises.explanation: Change final a to o: sana → sano-; add -jen to get sanojen. Keep strong nt and change a to o: hinta → hinto-; add -jen.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: muna (“egg”); kesä (“summer”).
exercises.explanation: Drop final a and add -ien: mun + ien = munien. Drop final ä and add -ien: kes + ien = kesien.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: nimi (“name”); vesi (“water”).
exercises.explanation: Use nimi- before -en: nimi + en = nimien. Use vesi- before -en: vesi + en = vesien. Plural vesi can refer to bodies of water.

exercises.prompt: Recall the plural genitives in order, separated by a comma: leipä (“bread”); ranta (“shore”).
exercises.explanation: Keep strong p, drop ä, and add -ien: leip + ien = leipien. Keep nt, change a to o, and add -jen: ranto + jen = rantojen.
